title: A cycle-wide product of block exponents produces a closure separation that exact integer dynamics cannot realize
statement: For a CycleMin word written as O^{a_i} E^{r_i} blocks, the product of rho_i = 3^{a_i}/2^{a_i+r_i}, together with local CycleMin constraints, yields an exponent balance or a sign obstruction that is not 3^o/2^L / cycle_itinerary_formally_expanding / global_defect_identity / image_eq_start_defectRatio / cycleMin_finance / leftover near-convergents of log 2 / log 3, and that obstruction empties or tightens a leftover length for a reason that is not finance.
counterexamples: ∏ rho_i = 3^A/2^{A+R} identically on (2,1)+(3,2)+(7,4) and on the single block (12,7)
the signed sum is o log 3 − L log 2 and ignores the partition
3^A = 2^{A+R} is impossible by unique factorization; that is cycle_itinerary_formally_expanding
exact return is Delta = n^{3^o} − n^{2^L} (global_defect_identity); floors are cycleMin_finance
L=19 OOE has rho=9/8 and rest 59049/65536 < 1; an expanding first block forces later contraction, not a global sign kill
notes: Phase 0 only. Not a finance leftover-killer and not a floor raise. The budget is a REPARAMETERIZATION of 3^o/2^L. No K=11, no L=55293, no Paper A edit, no ledger row, no new Lean. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: algebraic identities on one three-block word; leftover lengths 19 and 84 with an OOE first block
